purpose: English rear-access wall repair discussion and illustrated crew handoff; preserve existing travertine.
owner_assumption: Assume the next RF05 form fits and centers correctly. This is a scenario, not a recorded physical pass.
scope: Local stable support and a shower-spray exclusion detail. No new CAD, owner survey, emails, purchases or physical tests.
recommendation: Mechanically supported cementitious infill, formed from the rear, followed by a smooth supported custom plate with a continuous stone-compatible perimeter seal and the retained factory foam/trim. The repair mortar and support are not themselves a waterproof barrier.
site_decisions: Identify sound cementitious substrate and permanent support from rear access; no reliance on crumbly board, stone-edge adhesion or unsupported wire.

Identify the existing water-management layer and any damaged boundary. Restore a compatible connection if accessible. A local plate seal does not certify restoration of an inaccessible concealed membrane.
Choose a backing/lath attachment and mortar embedment compatible with the actual available depth, framing, pipes, service access and intended repair product.
Rehearse the lined form's release, including the rear collar reliefs. Maximum collar depth is not permissible fill depth. Keep repair out of reliefs, tabs, rods and central service cavity.
Confirm adhesion/nonstaining of the actual stone, sealant and final metal finish, with a workable joint cross-section and curing sequence.

inferences: The contractor's mention of wire may mean expanded metal lath; his intended method is not known.
The rear photographs show access and obstructions but do not identify all layers or a continuous waterproof membrane.
A plate perimeter seal outside damage plus the complete factory gasket is a maintainable local spray barrier concept, not proof of entire-shower waterproofing.
A framed cementitious backer is preferable to relying on an unsupported mortar lip; exact anchorage and reinforcement cover must be set at the exposed wall.
